title: Theorem thm:S0 (mod-p^2 evaluation of S_0) is cited, not proved — blocks all established parts

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Section 4, Theorem `thm:S0` ("This is a known supercongruence ... We take Theorem~\ref{thm:S0} as a cited input").

**Gap.** The mod-$p^2$ evaluation
$$S_0=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\binom{2k}{k}^3/16^k\equiv 4x^2-2p\ (p\equiv1\bmod6,\,p=x^2+3y^2),\qquad S_0\equiv0\ (p\equiv5\bmod6)\pmod{p^2}$$
is asserted as a citation and never proved. This is the load-bearing input of the whole established part of the solution:
- Part (i.1) IS exactly `thm:S0`(1).
- Part (ii) ($S_0\equiv0$, $S_1\equiv p/3$) is deduced from `thm:S0`(2) + the linking identity.
- The refutation of (i.2) ($S_1\equiv(3p-4x^2)/3$) is deduced from `thm:S0`(1) + the linking identity.

Hence with `thm:S0` unproved, NONE of (i.1),(ii) and not even the refutation of (i.2) is actually established; all are conditional on a black box.

**What must be proved.** A genuine proof of the mod-$p^2$ supercongruence for $\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\binom{2k}{k}^3/16^k$ in terms of the CM datum $x$ of $p=x^2+3y^2$. Standard routes: (a) identify the truncated ${}_3F_2(1/2,1/2,1/2;1,1)$ with a Greene $\mathbb F_p$-hypergeometric function, evaluate via a Jacobi-sum formula tied to the elliptic curve with CM by $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$, then lift to $\mathbb Z/p^2$ by a Dwork-type congruence; or (b) Gross--Koblitz + a second-order $\Gamma_p$ expansion. Each named theorem must be stated precisely and its hypotheses verified.

**Status:** numerics confirm the target congruence is TRUE (verified $p\le100$); the gap is that it is unproved, not that it is wrong.
